data.name: Dhristika
data.gender_notes: Dhristika is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Dhristika is derived from the Sanskrit root dhri which means ‘to hold’ or ‘to see’. The name signifies one who has a clear vision, one who can discern truth and wisdom. The name Dhristika carries the meaning “View, Sight, Vision” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dhristika usually hope their child will grow to embody view, sight, vision and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embodiment of clear vision and insight.
data.etymology: Dhristika belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “View, Sight, Vision.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dhristika total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

It is a name that reflects an individual's dedication to seeking knowledge, understanding the truth, and living a wise and enlightened life.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Dhristika represents an individual's internal quest for knowledge, wisdom, and truth. historical_references.reference: The Hindu goddess Dhristika, also known as Dhritashtra's wife Krishnaa or Draupadi, was an important figure in the Hindu epic Mahabharata. She is famously known for her role in the Mahabharata war and the subsequent curse that led to the great battle.

Another reference to Dhristika can be found in the Puranic texts, where she is described as the goddess of truth and the wife of the sun god, Surya. She is also known to grant boons to those who worship her.
